name: Spain 2010-12 (Del Bosque)
scopeNote: Spain under Vicente del Bosque only, from the 2010 World Cup opener (0-1 v Switzerland, Durban, 16 June 2010; Irish Times) to the Euro 2012 final (4-0 v Italy, 1 July 2012; FourFourTwo). Counted: 2010 World Cup finals, Euro 2012 qualifying (Group I, Sept 2010-Nov 2011) and Euro 2012 finals. NOT counted: Luis Aragones and Euro 2008, and Del Bosque's first two years (appointed mid-July 2008, first match friendly v Denmark 20 Aug 2008, first competitive match WC qualifier v Bosnia 6 Sept 2008) including the 2010 World Cup qualifying and 2009 Confederations Cup, because the brief frames the profile as World Cup 2010 to Euro 2012; the style was the same (Del Bosque: 'a style created in 2008'). Appointment day (15 July 2008) is only in search summaries, not on a mined page. Style term used by sources: possession game / tiki-taka (press label; Del Bosque said 'no magic formula') and, at Euro 2012, a strikerless 'false nine' 4-6-0 (Football Espana) while Cox says the final was not a 4-6-0 because Fabregas ran like a true centre-forward. 2010 shape: 4-2-3-1/4-3-3 hybrid with Busquets-Alonso double pivot, Xavi ahead, Villa left, Torres/Pedro. Marking: no verified source on zonal v man at set pieces for this period; open-play defending is described as collective cover, not man-marking (Pique on Ronaldo). Possession figure for the final is Opta/Stats Zone 56.6%. Pre-2010 and post-2012 items (Oct 2012 France, 2014 Marca, 2016 Publico) kept unverified or as statedView only.
openQuestions: Zonal v man-marking at corners/free-kicks for Spain 2010-12 not found in any readable source (FIFA 2022 report says Spain used player-to-player in 2022, which is outside period).
Appointment date 15 July 2008 not confirmed on a mined page (RTE article is dated around 15 July 2008 but gives only debut 20 Aug and first competitive match 6 Sept 2008).
Euro 2012 final possession: Stats Zone 56.6% (FourFourTwo) conflicts with another Stats Zone figure of 65.9% seen only in a search summary.
Pressing after loss (counter-press) is described by Wilson (2010) and Libertad Digital (2012) but not quantified; no PPDA/Opta source found.
Popular label 4-6-0: Football Espana uses it, Cox says the final was not 4-6-0; the strikerless system was used in the group v Italy, v France, and in the final, but not v Ireland, Croatia, Portugal.
UEFA technical report on Euro 2012 and soccer-spain.com WC 2010 match report not accessible.
Whether Euro 2012 qualifying friendly-style matches and the 2010 WC qualifiers should be counted is a user decision; second-order effect on the profile is small (same XI core).
